title: PREM: Prefix-Steered Recurrent Memory for Long-Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2609.23601v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long-video understanding must capture transient visual evidence under strict token budgets, yet existing methods compress frames, append memory tokens, or alter internal key-value (KV) caches. We introduce Prefix-Steered Recurrent Memory (PREM), a memory-token-free framework for frozen vision-language models (VLMs). PREM separates video ingestion from query answering: a recurrent writer distills visual streams into a compact 256 KiB multi-slot associative state, while a question-conditioned readout adds memory-derived key/value (K/V) steering modulations to existing non-visual prompt prefixes during prefill. This enables write-once, query-many inference without extra prompt tokens or decoding recurrence. Across six long-video benchmarks in offline and streaming end-of-stream settings, PREM consistently outperforms frozen baselines at every evaluated visual budget. Under a constrained budget of 16 frames, PREM improves macro-average acc

translated_title: PREM：面向长视频理解的前缀引导循环记忆
translated_abstract: 长视频理解需要在严格的token预算下捕获瞬态视觉证据，然而现有方法要么压缩视频帧、追加记忆token，要么修改内部的键值（KV）缓存。我们提出了前缀引导循环记忆，这是一个面向冻结视觉语言模型（VLM）的无记忆token框架。PREM将视频摄取与查询应答分离：一个循环写入器将视觉流提炼为紧凑的256 KiB多槽关联状态，同时一个问题条件化的读取器在预填充阶段向现有的非视觉提示前缀添加由记忆导出的键/值（K/V）引导调制。这使得推理能够实现“一次写入、多次查询”，而无需额外的提示token或解码阶段的循环计算。在离线和流式端到端设置下的六个长视频基准测试中，PREM在所有评估的视觉预算下均持续优于冻结基线。在16帧的受限预算下，PREM提高了宏平均准确率（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: PREM提出了一种无需记忆token的框架，通过循环写入器将视频流压缩为紧凑的多槽关联状态，并在预填充阶段以记忆导出的键值调制引导冻结视觉语言模型，实现“一次写入、多次查询”的高效长视频理解。
en_tdlr: PREM is a memory-token-free framework that distills video streams into a compact 256 KiB multi-slot associative state via a recurrent writer and steers frozen VLMs with memory-derived K/V modulations on prompt prefixes during prefill, enabling write-once, query-many long-video understanding.
